stem:
Johnny is a 10-year-old boy en route to the emergency department after a high-speed bicycle crash. He was apparently knocked unconscious. On assessment, his right pupil is 3 mm and briskly reactive to light, while his left pupil is 8 mm and non-reactive. He has a large swelling on the right side of his head.

Which one of the following is suggested by these clinical findings?
explanation: A unilateral dilated, non-reactive pupil after head trauma is concerning for a focal intracranial process causing increased intracranial pressure, such as an evolving intracranial haemorrhage with impending uncal herniation. This is a neurosurgical emergency.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

rationale: The combination of head trauma, reduced conscious level, and an ipsilateral dilated non-reactive pupil is a classic red flag for raised intracranial pressure from an expanding intracranial lesion.

optionExplanations.A: A lazy eye (amblyopia) does not cause an acutely fixed dilated pupil after trauma.
optionExplanations.B: Migraine can cause visual symptoms but does not explain an acutely unilateral fixed dilated pupil in this context.
optionExplanations.C: Eye trauma can affect the pupil, but the overall scenario strongly suggests an intracranial cause after head injury.
optionExplanations.D: Shock may cause poor perfusion, but it does not typically produce a unilateral fixed dilated pupil.
optionExplanations.E: Correct: a unilateral fixed dilated pupil after head injury suggests raised intracranial pressure/third nerve compression.

source.quizTitle: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury
source.questionTextHtml:
This information suggests Johnny's conscious level is deteriorating. As part of your neurological assessment, you review Johnny’s pupils:

His right pupil measures 3mm and reacts briskly to light

His left pupil measures 8mm and does not appear reactive

You notice a large swelling at the right side of Johnny’s head.

Which one of the following is suggested by these clinical findings?
source.stimulusText:
2

Clinical scenario 1 - Johnny

Teaching/Learning points:

Rapid neurological assessment

GCS including AVPU and Modified GCS

Prevention of secondary insult

Johnny is a 10 year old boy. He is en-route to the emergency department via ambulance following a fall from his bike. Paramedics have called ahead, stating Johnny was riding downhill and hit the side of a parked car at the bottom. He was thrown over the car, landing on the street. He was not wearing a helmet and was apparently knocked unconscious.

He is described as semi-conscious, breathing at a rate of 18/min, sats 98% in air, heart rate 90pbm. He has a large swelling to the right side of his head, and no other obvious injuries. Their ETA is 15 minutes.

The following ten questions refer to Johnny’s clinical scenario.
